First things first, the OG @StovallCFRA has shared this for years, so shout out to him for this one.

It took 23 trading days for the S&P 500 to be down 5% from the Oct 6th ATH.

Sam found that most bear markets started with a quick move down 5% from ATHs. In fact, only one bear market ever (34% in late '60s/early '70) took longer than 23 trading days to hit down 5%.

Could this go into a full fledged bear market? Of course it could, but for now we don't expect that and this suggests don't panic just yet.

US put option trading volume on CBOE surged to a record 11.23 million contracts on Thursday.

As a result, the 20-day average of put option volume rose to ~7 million contracts, near its highest on record.

By comparison, the 20-day average oscillated around 4 million contracts in 2022.

8 of the 10 highest daily put option volume readings have occurred in 2026.

We are seeing unprecedented options activity right now.

“Founded by Ben and Felicia Horowitz, the Paid in Full Foundation honors the hip-hop immortals whose artistic contributions far outweigh the financial remuneration they received in return.”

“As Ben described Eric B. & Rakim’s debut masterpiece, the foundation’s namesake Paid in Full: ‘I bought it for $10 and got at least $5 million worth of value out of it. It needed to be paid back.’”

“Each honoree receives a five-year grant with no strings attached. Inspired by Quincy Jones’ work with the Jazz Foundation, the grants have allowed past recipients, among them Rakim, Scarface, George Clinton, Roxanne Shanté, Grandmaster Caz, Kool Moe Dee, Grand Puba, and Kool G Rap, to purchase homes, pay off medical bills, and finish long-delayed creative projects.”

“Of course, a few grants a year can’t repay an entire generation, but they’re a start. Paid in Full refuses to let these cultural giants languish in our midst, and its grants have fundamentally changed the artists’ lives, though still not as much as the artists changed ours.”

tweets.text:
BREAKING: US nonfarm labor productivity rose at a +3.5% annualized in Q3 2026, its largest increase since Q3 2025.

This also marks its 3rd consecutive quarterly improvement.

Nonfarm business output, which excludes the impact of government spending, surged at a +3.7% annualized rate, the strongest growth rate since Q3 2025.

Hourly compensation rose at a +2.9% annualized rate.

As productivity growth outpaced hourly compensation, unit labor costs, which measure labor costs per unit of output, declined -0.7% last quarter, the first quarterly decline since Q2 2025.

This largely a product of companies investing heavily in AI, software, and equipment to improve efficiency, increase output, and contain labor expenses.

AI is catalyzing a major US productivity surge.

Employee compensation is 59.6% of US personal income, down from about 73% around 1970.

Transfer payments, dividends, and rental income now make up 31.1%, more than double their share in the 1960s.

A weaker job market hits total household income less than it used to. https://t.co/WriOt5TImk

Hiring is improving slightly. Layoffs remain very low. https://t.co/bBbtlrgvaa
